tools.name: dp_search
tools.description: Start here for a general privacy question. One keyword search across the whole hub: directory tools, how-to guides, curated tool stacks and the glossary. Use 1–3 keywords such as 'vpn', 'data broker' or 'grapheneos'; every keyword must match, and filler words like 'how', 'best' and 'private' are ign

tools.name: dp_search_tools
tools.description: Use when a user wants privacy tool recommendations (VPNs, email, browsers, messengers, password managers, etc.). Matches records containing every query word, so 1–2 keywords such as 'vpn' or 'password manager' work and a full sentence usually returns nothing. For a whole kind of tool, use `category`

tools.name: dp_get_tool
tools.description: Fetch one directory tool's full record by slug: description, DP pick (if any), jurisdiction, encryption, PII requirements, platforms, and its Default Privacy page (dp_url). Also returns `sources` (links, keyed by the field they back, with the date checked) and `caveats` (things to know before choosi

tools.name: dp_list_categories
tools.description: List the privacy tool directory's category groups and subcategories with tool counts. Use the returned slugs to filter dp_search_tools.

tools.name: dp_find_alternatives
tools.description: Use when a user wants to replace a mainstream product: consumer apps and services (Gmail, WhatsApp, Chrome, Google Drive, Zoom, LastPass, Windows…) or a website tracker / ad script (Google Analytics, Hotjar, Mixpanel, Facebook Pixel…). Pass the product's name. Trackers return a curated swap list. Co

tools.name: dp_get_related_tools
tools.description: Use after dp_get_tool for 'what else is like X?': returns other tools in the same directory category with DP picks first, then A to Z, excluding X. X must be a directory slug; for a product the directory doesn't list, use dp_find_alternatives.

tools.name: dp_compare_tools
tools.description: Fetch the full Privacy Protocol records for 2–5 tools by slug for side-by-side comparison (DP pick, jurisdiction, encryption, PII requirements), each with `sources` and `caveats`. A null field means Default Privacy has not checked it (never read null as no); quote the caveats and cite the sources. U

tools.name: dp_search_guides
tools.description: Search Default Privacy's long-form privacy how-tos, e.g. switching to GrapheneOS, keeping a home address off people-search sites, data-broker removal, running your own VPN, and the 'How to Live Privately' series. Filter by category. Returns metadata and links; use dp_get_guide for full content.

tools.name: dp_get_guide
tools.description: Fetch a single guide's full markdown content and metadata by slug.

tools.name: dp_list_stacks
tools.description: List every privacy stack: a curated set of directory tools for one goal or threat (a privacy starter kit, de-Googling, leaving Gmail, a journalist's or a stalking survivor's kit, Windows hardening…). Returns title, slug, a short description and url for each; use dp_get_stack for one stack's full con

tools.name: dp_get_stack
tools.description: Fetch one privacy stack's full markdown content and metadata by slug: the tools in setup order, why each one, and the tradeoffs. Slugs come from dp_list_stacks or dp_search.

tools.name: dp_route
tools.description: Describe the user's situation or goal in their own words (e.g. "I'm a journalist protecting sources", "I just bought a Pixel and want GrapheneOS", "which password manager", "I want to use AI more privately") and get the best-matching Default Privacy situations, each with the guides and stacks to rea

tools.name: dp_check_mcp_server
tools.description: Before connecting an MCP server, check whether it is in Default Privacy's vetted list and what it can read or change. Give its repository URL, server URL, name or slug. A listed server returns its record with sources and caveats. An unlisted one returns a short checklist; unlisted is not a verdict,

tools.name: dp_search_glossary
tools.description: Search the privacy & security glossary for defined terms. Returns term, definition, and link; use dp_get_glossary_term for the full entry.

tools.name: dp_get_glossary_term
tools.description: Fetch a single glossary term's full definition and content by slug.

tools.name: dp_check_email_security
tools.description: Check a domain's email authentication posture — SPF, DKIM, and DMARC DNS records — and return an A–F grade with explanations. Read-only DNS lookups; no email is sent or stored.

tools.name: dp_check_whois_privacy
tools.description: Look up a domain's public WHOIS/RDAP registration record and flag exposed personal identity fields (registrant name, email, phone, address). Read-only RDAP lookup.

tools.name: dp_check_domain_breaches
tools.description: Check whether a domain appears in known public data breaches (via the Have I Been Pwned breach catalog). Returns matching breaches with dates, exposed data classes, and account counts. Domain-level only — no personal email is queried.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.defaultprivacy.com" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: dp_search, dp_search_tools, dp_find_alternatives, dp_list_stacks, dp_check_mcp_server, dp_check_email_security, dp_check_whois_privacy, dp_check_domain_breaches · Private data: dp_search, dp_search_tools, dp_get_tool, dp_find_alternatives, dp_compare_tools, dp_route, dp_check_mcp_server, dp_check_email_security, dp_check_whois_privacy · Public sink: dp_search_tools, dp_check_email_security, dp_check_whois_privacy, dp_check_domain_breaches.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: dp_search, dp_search_tools, dp_find_alternatives, dp_list_stacks, dp_check_mcp_server, dp_check_email_security, dp_check_whois_privacy, dp_check_domain_breaches · Private data: dp_search, dp_search_tools, dp_get_tool, dp_find_alternatives, dp_compare_tools, dp_route, dp_check_mcp_server, dp_check_email_security, dp_check_whois_privacy · Public sink: dp_search_tools, dp_check_email_security, dp_check_whois_privacy, dp_check_domain_breaches

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
